title: Unemployment Benefit Claims — Family Rates per Dependent on a Dependency Redetermination
content:
For a dependency redetermination on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record, the per-dependent amount — the weekly amount multiplied by the dependents counted to give the redetermined dependency allowance — is set by the number of dependents on record and the age of the claim.

The age of the claim is the number of calendar days from the claim effective date to the handling date.

## Rate schedule

| Dependents on record | Claim effective date | Per-dependent amount (USD per week) |
|---|---|---|
| Two or more | At least 182 calendar days before the handling date | 18.00 (long-claim family amount) |
| Two or more | Fewer than 182 calendar days before the handling date | 16.00 (short-claim family amount) |
| Fewer than two | Any | The program's own per-dependent amount |

Any other dependency redetermination uses the program's per-dependent amount.

## Both sides of the 182-day line

| Hypothetical case | Dependents on record | Age of the claim | Per-dependent amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 2 | 182 days | 18.00 |
| B | 2 | 181 days | 16.00 |
| C | 1 | 300 days | The program's own per-dependent amount |

### Hypothetical figure

With 3 dependents on record, a claim 200 days old and a program maximum of 3 dependents counted, the per-dependent amount is 18.00, and 18.00 times the 3 dependents counted is 54.00.
